Controlled PDF & Document Creation Guideline
Document ID: DOC-STD-001 Domain: Document control, records management and PDF publishing
Document status: Sample guideline — draft for organisational adaptation
Intended use: Enterprise / PSU / refinery / industrial RAG knowledge base
Purpose
Establish a consistent, reviewable method for preparing, approving, exporting, distributing and revising
business-critical PDF documents in a public-sector enterprise, refinery, process plant or industrial organisation.

Important: This document is an illustrative, generic template created for LUMI RAG testing. It is not issued, endorsed or
approved by any named PSU, refinery, regulator or standards body. Before operational use, the organisation must review it
against its current policies, applicable law, approved procedures, contracts and site-specific requirements. Terminology
MUST = mandatory within this sample guideline once formally adopted. SHOULD = recommended practice. MUST
NOT = prohibited practice. CHECK = release or validation check. RAG = instructions for retrieval-augmented
generation. 1.

Applicability and authority
RULE This guideline is a generic internal-control template. It is not an official requirement of any PSU, refinery,
regulator or standards body. The organisation's approved document-control procedure, retention schedule, security
classification and legal requirements take precedence. MUST Every controlled document must have an identifiable owner, document title, unique document number,
revision identifier, issue date and approval status. MUST Drafts, approved-for-use documents and obsolete documents must be visibly distinguishable.

MUST NOT Do not present an unapproved draft as an approved procedure, specification, engineering instruction or
policy. 2. Document identification and metadata
MUST Use the organisation's approved document-numbering convention. If none is supplied, use a clearly marked
provisional identifier and do not invent a corporate numbering scheme. MUST Show document title, document number, revision, status, issue date, originating department and page number
in the document control area. SHOULD Include preparer, technical reviewer, approver and approval dates in a revision or approval table.

MUST Record the source of technical values, drawings, tables and external references. MUST NOT Invent approval names, signatures, dates, document numbers or controlled-copy stamps. 3. Page layout and readability
SHOULD Use A4 portrait for ordinary reports and correspondence. Use landscape only when wide tables, drawings
or forms require it. SHOULD Use consistent margins, heading hierarchy, paragraph spacing and page numbering throughout the
document. MUST Ensure tables, figures, footnotes and warnings are not clipped, overlapped or rendered outside page
boundaries.
MUST Use legible fonts and sufficient contrast. Do not communicate status using colour alone.

LUMI RAG SAMPLE KNOWLEDGE BASE • GENERIC TEMPLATE • VERIFY BEFORE ADOPTION Page 2
SHOULD Keep headers and footers consistent and include a short document identifier and revision where
appropriate. 4. PDF export and accessibility
MUST Export to PDF from the approved source document or a validated generation process. Reopen the exported
PDF and inspect it before release. MUST Verify page count, page order, text extraction, hyperlinks, tables, figures and special characters after export. SHOULD Use searchable text rather than image-only pages whenever the source permits.

SHOULD Use tagged headings, meaningful reading order, descriptive link text and document language metadata
where the PDF tool supports them. MUST If a scanned document is unavoidable, apply OCR and visually verify critical names, values, units, document
numbers and dates. MUST NOT Treat successful file creation as proof that the PDF is complete, readable or correct. 5. Approval and release
MUST Route the document to the designated technical and document-control reviewers before controlled release. MUST Record approval evidence in the approved workflow.

A typed name or generated signature image is not a
substitute for an authorised approval process. MUST Release only the approved revision to the controlled repository or distribution list. MUST Mark superseded copies as obsolete or withdrawn according to the organisation's records procedure. MUST NOT Overwrite an approved historical revision without preserving the required record. 6. Confidentiality and distribution
MUST Apply the organisation's information-classification and handling rules before creating, exporting or distributing
a PDF.

MUST Remove unintended comments, tracked changes, hidden content and document metadata when required by
the approved sanitisation procedure. MUST Check that the recipient list and distribution channel are authorised for the document classification. MUST NOT Upload restricted plant, personnel, security or commercially sensitive information to an unapproved
external service. 7. Final pre-release checklist
CHECK Correct title, document number, revision, status and date. CHECK All required reviews and approvals are recorded. CHECK Page numbers, tables, figures, units and references are correct.

CHECK PDF opens, is searchable where expected and has no clipped or missing content. CHECK Classification, metadata, comments and distribution permissions are appropriate. CHECK Obsolete revisions are handled according to document-control procedure. 8. RAG application instructions
RAG For a request to create a PDF report, retrieve this guideline together with any applicable report template,
records procedure and security-classification policy. RAG Apply layout, metadata, export-verification and release-checklist rules.

Do not invent organisation-specific
document numbers, approvers, classifications or retention periods.

Technical Report & Engineering Document
Guideline
Document ID: ENG-STD-002 Domain: Engineering reports, technical studies and plant documentation
Document status: Sample guideline — draft for organisational adaptation
Intended use: Enterprise / PSU / refinery / industrial RAG knowledge base
Purpose
Provide a disciplined structure for engineering reports used in refineries, process plants, utilities, terminals,
manufacturing facilities and public-sector engineering organisations.

Important: This document is an illustrative, generic template created for LUMI RAG testing. It is not issued, endorsed or
approved by any named PSU, refinery, regulator or standards body. Before operational use, the organisation must review it
against its current policies, applicable law, approved procedures, contracts and site-specific requirements. Terminology
MUST = mandatory within this sample guideline once formally adopted. SHOULD = recommended practice. MUST
NOT = prohibited practice. CHECK = release or validation check. RAG = instructions for retrieval-augmented
generation. 1.

Governing principle
RULE This is a generic drafting guideline, not an approved engineering standard. Applicable statutory requirements,
site engineering practices, approved design bases and discipline-specific standards must be checked by competent
personnel. MUST Distinguish measured data, calculated results, assumptions, estimates, vendor information and engineering
judgement. MUST NOT Present an assumption, preliminary calculation or unverified field observation as a confirmed plant fact. 2.

Standard report structure
MUST Include title, document identifier if assigned, revision, date, originating discipline, authoring team and review
status. SHOULD Use the following sections where relevant: Executive Summary; Purpose; Scope; References; Existing
Conditions; Methodology; Data and Assumptions; Findings; Engineering Assessment; Risks and Limitations;
Recommendations; Conclusion; Appendices. MUST State the question being answered and the boundary of the assessment.

SHOULD Put decision-critical findings and required actions in the executive summary without replacing the detailed
technical basis. 3. Technical data and calculations
MUST Show units for every engineering quantity and use a consistent unit system within each calculation. MUST Identify data source, date, operating condition, instrument tag or drawing reference where available. MUST State assumptions, boundary conditions, calculation method, input values and relevant limitations. MUST Check dimensional consistency and independently verify critical calculations.

SHOULD Use tables for comparable operating values and charts for trends. Label axes, units, time period and data
source. MUST NOT Create plausible-looking operating data, equipment ratings, process conditions or performance figures
when they were not supplied.

LUMI RAG SAMPLE KNOWLEDGE BASE • GENERIC TEMPLATE • VERIFY BEFORE ADOPTION Page 2
4. Drawings, diagrams and equipment references
MUST Use current approved drawings where available and record drawing number and revision. MUST Label equipment, lines, instruments and boundaries consistently with the source material. MUST Mark conceptual or illustrative diagrams as NOT FOR CONSTRUCTION or equivalent when appropriate. MUST NOT Modify an engineering drawing and imply that the modified version is an approved plant drawing.

SHOULD Include legends, units, north/reference direction and revision information where relevant. 5. Findings, recommendations and actions
MUST Link each recommendation to a stated finding, evidence source or identified risk. SHOULD Assign an action owner, priority and target date only when these are known or explicitly agreed. MUST Separate mandatory corrective actions from optional improvement opportunities. MUST State unresolved data gaps and the impact they have on the conclusion. MUST NOT Claim that a recommendation is approved, implemented or risk-reducing without evidence. 6.

Review and technical assurance
MUST Identify the required discipline reviewers and competent approver according to the site's workflow. MUST Check calculations, units, references, drawing revisions, data provenance and conclusions before issue. SHOULD Use independent checking for safety-critical, design-critical or high-consequence calculations as required
by site procedure. MUST Record review comments and their disposition in the approved document-control system. 7.

RAG application instructions
RAG For engineering reports, retrieve this guideline plus relevant discipline procedures, approved design bases,
drawing registers and project-specific templates. RAG Use only supplied or retrieved verified technical values. Preserve source references beside values and
conclusions. RAG If critical plant data, equipment tags, design conditions or approved standards are missing, flag the gap and
request competent review rather than inventing values.

CORPORATE PRESENTATION
GUIDELINES
A practical standard for professional presentations in PSU-style and public-sector organisations
Purpose Create consistent, credible, decision-oriented presentations for management, technical, project and
stakeholder communication. Audience Executives, board and committee members, government stakeholders, project teams, engineers and
external partners. Applicability General guidance for organisations with formal governance, public accountability and technical
operations. Internal policies take precedence.

CORE PRINCIPLE
A corporate presentation is an official communication and decision-support document—not a
brochure. It should be accurate, restrained, traceable to evidence, easy to navigate and explicit
about the action or decision required. General guidance | Version 1.0 | November 2026

Corporate Presentation Guidelines | General PSU-style standard Page 2
1. The standard at a glance
l Purpose before design: define audience, objective and required outcome before creating slides. l One message per slide: make the title state the conclusion, not merely the topic. l Evidence over assertion: show sources, periods, units, assumptions and data status. l Formal, not flashy: use restrained colours, consistent layouts and meaningful visuals. l Decision-ready: state the issue, options, implications, recommendation, owner and next step.

l Controlled information: classify, review and distribute in line with organisational rules. 2. Plan before creating slides
l Identify the audience: board/committee, senior management, ministry or government department, technical
reviewers, project teams, vendors or the public. l State the objective: inform, seek approval, review performance, explain a technical issue, obtain funding or
report progress. l Define the ask: write the exact decision, approval, guidance or action expected.

l Choose the level of detail: keep essential messages in the main deck; move calculations, detailed tables
and drawings to an appendix. l Set the time budget: plan slide count around speaking time and leave room for questions. l Build a storyline: context → current position → evidence → options/risks → recommendation →
decision/action.

Typical main-deck length
Presentation type Typical range Emphasis
Executive / board decision 8–15 slides Decision, impact, risks, recommendation
Monthly / quarterly review 8–18 slides Targets vs actuals, variance, corrective action
Project progress review 10–20 slides Milestones, schedule, cost, scope, risks
Technical / engineering review 10–20 slides Requirements, design basis, options, calculations, safety
Corporate overview 8–12 slides Mandate, operations, footprint, performance, priorities
These are planning aids, not mandatory limits.
Follow meeting instructions and organisational requirements.

Corporate Presentation Guidelines | General PSU-style standard Page 3
3. Recommended structure for a formal deck
l Title: presentation title, business unit/project, meeting/forum, presenter and date; use approved identity. l Purpose and decision required: why the presentation is being made and what is expected. l Executive summary: three to five key messages, current status and principal recommendation. l Background and context: mandate, scope, prior decisions, baseline or project stage. l Current position: performance, progress or technical status against approved baseline.

l Evidence and analysis: metrics, trends, variance, options and supporting analysis. l Risks and constraints: safety, schedule, cost, procurement, regulatory, environmental and operational risks,
as relevant. l Recommendation / way forward: preferred option, rationale, resources and expected impact. l Decision and action points: approvals sought, responsible owner, due date and dependencies. l Appendix: calculations, assumptions, definitions, references, data tables and supplementary material. 4.

Slide design and visual standards
l Approved identity: follow the official logo, brand colours, typefaces, template and disclaimer rules. Never
distort a logo. l Restrained palette: one primary corporate colour, one supporting colour, neutral backgrounds and limited
highlights. Define red/amber/green consistently. l Consistent layouts: align titles, body text, footers, page numbers, charts and margins. l Readable typography: practical starting point: 28–36 pt titles, 18–24 pt body text; avoid going below 14 pt for
essential content. l Whitespace: do not fill every area.

A slide should be understandable at a glance. l Relevant visuals: use accurate, authorised photographs, maps, process diagrams, engineering drawings and
charts. l Avoid decoration: excessive gradients, shadows, 3D charts, spinning transitions, clip art, emoji and
ornamental icons. l Animation: use only when it explains a sequence or reveals information deliberately. The PDF export should
still make sense. Slide-density test
If the audience must read paragraphs while listening, the slide is probably too dense. Split it, simplify it or move
detail to the appendix.

Do not fix density by shrinking the font. 5. Writing style and official language
l Use clear, neutral, precise and professional language. Prefer plain English over jargon, slogans and
promotional claims. l Expand abbreviations on first use or provide a glossary. Keep terminology consistent across projects, assets,
departments and units. l Avoid unsupported claims such as 'best', 'world-class' or '100% successful'. Quantify claims and provide
evidence. l Separate facts, estimates, assumptions, forecasts, proposals and opinions. Label them clearly.

l Use unambiguous dates (for example, 23 November 2026) and consistent number formatting. l Avoid casual language, memes, informal stock imagery and unapproved external branding. 6. Data, charts and financial information

Corporate Presentation Guidelines | General PSU-style standard Page 4
l Show the basis: identify source/system, reporting period, extraction date, unit, scope, definitions and
exclusions. l Compare like with like: use the same period, unit, denominator, scope and method for comparisons. l Show target and actual: where relevant, display approved target/baseline, actual, variance and status. l Explain variance carefully: distinguish measured causes from hypotheses; do not infer causation from
correlation alone. l Label charts: descriptive title, axes, units, period, legend and source.

Avoid misleading scales or cropped
axes. l Choose suitable charts: lines for trends, bars for comparisons, stacked bars for composition and tables for
exact values. l Financial discipline: specify currency, actual/budget/estimate status, tax treatment where relevant, price
base, capex/opex and assumptions. l Reconcile totals: ensure totals, percentages and chart labels agree with source records. l Mark provisional data: label unaudited, estimated, preliminary and forecast figures prominently. Suggested data caption
Source: [system/report], extracted [date]. Period: [start–end]. Unit: [unit].

Scope: [sites/assets
included]. Note: [definition, exclusion or assumption].

Corporate Presentation Guidelines | General PSU-style standard Page 5
7. Technical, engineering and project presentations
l State design basis, scope boundaries, applicable standards/codes and revision status. l Identify source and revision of drawings, specifications, calculations and technical documents. Do not present
superseded documents as current. l Show units consistently; state assumptions, operating conditions, tolerances and limitations. l For calculations, show governing equation, input values, units, method, result and check. Put detailed
derivations in the appendix.

l Distinguish design values, measured values, vendor data, estimates and field observations. l For project reviews, report scope, schedule, cost, quality, safety, procurement, commissioning and
dependencies as relevant. l Use approved risk registers and status definitions. Include owner, mitigation, due date and residual exposure
where material. l A presentation is not a substitute for a signed engineering approval, statutory submission, controlled drawing
or formal technical record. 8.

Governance, confidentiality and public-sector sensitivity
l Follow the organisation's information-security policy, records-retention rules, approved templates and
delegated approval matrix. l Apply only the classification marking authorised by the organisation. Do not invent labels such as 'Confidential'
or 'Restricted'. l Do not include personal, commercially sensitive, procurement-sensitive, security or third-party confidential
information unless necessary and authorised.

l Verify permissions before including facility photographs, critical-infrastructure details, employee images,
maps, operational screens or security arrangements. l Use approved, attributable sources for policy, legal, regulatory, financial and performance claims. l Do not imply government endorsement, board approval, statutory clearance or management sign-off unless
formally documented. l Distinguish 'for information', 'for discussion', 'for recommendation' and 'for approval'. l Distribute through approved channels and control editable files and exports according to policy. 9.

Accessibility and room-readiness
l Maintain strong text/background contrast; do not rely on colour alone to communicate status. l Use descriptive chart labels and meaningful alternative text for important visuals where supported. l Avoid tiny text, dense tables, low-resolution images and difficult colour combinations. l Test on the actual presentation screen or a comparable display, not only on a laptop. l Check fonts, embedded media, hyperlinks, slide dimensions, page numbering and PDF export. l Prepare a static PDF backup; ensure key messages remain clear without animation or video.

l For hybrid meetings, test screen sharing, audio, video playback and remote readability. 10. Review, approval and version control
l Assign a content owner and a reviewer with appropriate subject-matter authority. l Check figures against the source of record; obtain finance, engineering, safety, legal, procurement or
communications review where needed.

Corporate Presentation Guidelines | General PSU-style standard Page 6
l Use the authorised approval route for board, committee, ministry, regulator or external stakeholder
presentations. l Record title, owner/business unit, date, version and status using the organisation's prescribed convention. l Use 'Draft' until approval is complete. A file export or automated quality check does not constitute approval. l Remove comments, tracked changes, hidden slides, speaker notes and metadata that should not be
distributed, subject to records policy.

l Keep a controlled final copy and archive supporting data and approvals according to policy. 11. Final quality-control checklist
Complete this review before presenting or distributing the deck. n The audience, purpose and required decision/action are explicit. n The executive summary matches the detailed slides. n The storyline is logical and fits the allotted time. n Important claims are supported by sources or labelled as assumptions/opinions. n Numbers, formulas, totals, units, dates and percentages have been checked.

n Charts have readable labels, correct scales, units, periods and sources. n Technical standards, drawing numbers and revisions are correct where applicable. n Risks, limitations, dependencies and unresolved issues are disclosed. n The approved corporate template, logo and visual identity are used correctly. n No unsupported approval, classification, endorsement or metadata is present. n Confidentiality, privacy, copyright and distribution permissions have been checked. n Spelling, grammar, alignment, slide numbering and PDF export have been reviewed.
n The final file opens correctly and has been tested on the presentation setup. 12.

Common mistakes to avoid
Avoid Use instead
Generic title: 'Project Update' Message title: 'Civil works are 2 weeks behind baseline'
Dense paragraphs copied from reports Short evidence-led bullets, charts and an appendix
Unexplained red/amber/green status Defined status thresholds, owner and next action
Chart without source or unit Chart with period, unit, source and labels
Recommendation without rationale Options, criteria, trade-offs and reasoned recommendation
Claim of approval without evidence Accurate status: draft, for discussion or formally approved
Decorative cover with no context Clean title slide followed by purpose and key messages
13.

Suggested master-slide layouts
l Title slide: approved logo, title, business unit, meeting, presenter and date. l Section divider: section title and optional one-line context. l Executive message: conclusion headline with three to five key points. l KPI dashboard: defined indicators with target, actual, variance and period. l Trend/comparison: chart with source and short interpretation.

Corporate Presentation Guidelines | General PSU-style standard Page 7
l Process/operating model: sequence, roles, interfaces and control points. l Project status: scope, schedule, cost, milestones, risks and decisions. l Decision slide: decision sought, options, recommendation, implications and approval route. l Appendix: legible detailed tables, calculations, references and technical details. 14. Applicability and precedence
These guidelines are a general professional baseline for PSU-style and other large public-sector organisations.

They do not replace an organisation's approved corporate identity manual, board/committee instructions,
government communication protocol, records policy, security classification scheme, procurement rules or
statutory requirements. Where a formal policy differs from this guide, follow the formal policy. END OF GUIDELINES

CORPORATE REPORTING &
DOCUMENTATION GUIDELINES
Internal management-reporting standard | Reference: CORP/STD/04 | Version 2.1
DOCUMENT STATUS: Synthetic test document prepared for evaluating L.U.M.I. document retrieval, analysis and report
generation. All names, figures and events are fictional.
Reporting period: October 2026 Issue date: 5 November 2026

BIEC | Synthetic demonstration material | Not an actual PSU record Page 2
1. Status and applicability
This synthetic guideline is the designated reporting reference for the L.U.M.I. test exercise. It applies to monthly
operational performance reports prepared for the General Manager, Director (Operations) or management review
committees at the fictional Bharat Industrial Engineering Corporation (BIEC). 2.

Mandatory report structure
Order Required section Minimum content
1 Cover page Organization, unit, report title, reporting
period, issuing department, document
reference and classification
2 Executive summary Key outcomes, material variances, critical
risks and decisions requested
3 Performance dashboard KPI name, target, actual, variance, unit and
status
4 Operational review Production, quality, equipment availability
and downtime
5 Maintenance and safety Preventive maintenance, breakdowns,
incidents and corrective actions
6 Energy and financial review Consumption, expenditure, budget utilization
and material variances
7 Projects Milestones, planned versus actual progress,
delays and dependencies
8 Risks and management actions Risk, impact, owner, priority and target date
9 Conclusion Overall assessment and decisions required
10 Annexures Definitions, source references and
supporting data
3.

Formatting standards
• Page size: A4 portrait for narrative pages; landscape pages may be used for wide tables. • Margins: 20 mm on all sides, with footer space reserved. • Typeface: Arial or an equivalent sans-serif font. Body text 10–11 pt; section headings 14–16 pt; table text not below 8
pt. • Use dark navy for primary headings and restrained grey or blue table headers. Avoid decorative backgrounds and
excessive color. • Use numbered section headings and consistent table numbering. Every table and chart must have a descriptive title.

• Include page numbers, report reference and document classification in the footer. • Use dates in DD Month YYYY format and Indian currency notation (n lakh or n crore) consistently. • Define abbreviations at first use. State units in table headers. 4. Analytical and evidence requirements
• Show planned and actual values together wherever both are available. • State the formula and denominator for calculated percentages.

BIEC | Synthetic demonstration material | Not an actual PSU record Page 3
• Distinguish source facts, calculations, management interpretation and recommendations. • Do not invent missing data, causal explanations, approvals or policy requirements. • Flag conflicting, incomplete or stale source records. Identify the source document and reporting period for material
figures. • Recommendations must include a responsible role and target date when those details are available; otherwise mark
them 'To be assigned'. 5.

Chart and table conventions
• Use bar charts for planned-versus-actual comparisons and line charts only when a time series is available. • Do not create trend lines from a single monthly observation. • Display units, labels and reporting period on every chart. • Avoid 3D charts. Ensure text and legends remain readable when printed. • Round percentages to one decimal place unless precision is material. 6. Classification and circulation
Use the classification 'INTERNAL — MANAGEMENT REVIEW' for this exercise. Circulate only to intended management
recipients.

Do not label a report 'Confidential', 'Secret' or with a statutory classification unless the issuing authority has
explicitly assigned that classification. 7. Approval and document control
The issuing department is responsible for checking source figures, confirming calculations and obtaining approval under
the organization's applicable delegation of authority. Record document reference, version, issue date and
preparer/reviewer roles where known. This guideline is synthetic and exists only to test retrieval-grounded formatting. It is not an actual government or PSU
standard.
